title: PixVerse Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits & Costs
summary: PixVerse pricing structures vary by subscription level, helping you determine which tier provides enough monthly credits for your specific video projects.
body_markdown:
## PixVerse vs Luma and Runway on value


PixVerse is the lowest entry point for commercial video rights among high-end generators, positioning it as the budget-efficient choice for you if you're a high-volume creator who prioritizes output quantity over brand-name prestige.


While competitors command a premium for cinematic aesthetics, PixVerse focuses on a utility-first pricing model that lowers the barrier to entry for your small-scale production.


### PixVerse vs Runway Gen-3 video quality


Runway Gen-3 remains the industry benchmark for physics-accurate motion and cinematic lighting, making it the preferred choice for high-end commercial work. If your project requires hyper-realistic human movement or complex fluid dynamics, Runway’s higher price point is justified by the reduced need for post-production cleanup.


Luma Dream Machine excels in spatial consistency, allowing for dramatic camera pans that maintain the 3D integrity of a scene better than most generators.


For filmmakers who need to simulate professional drone shots or complex tracking movements, Luma provides a level of architectural stability that PixVerse often struggles to match.


### Price per high-definition generation


PixVerse maintains a significant price advantage over its primary competitors, offering the most affordable path to professional-grade video assets.


If you're balancing tight production budgets against the need for high-resolution content, the monthly overhead for PixVerse is substantially lower than for equivalent tiers on other platforms.


Provider Pro-Tier Monthly Cost


PixVerse $30


Runway Gen-3 $35


Luma Dream Machine $90


Kling AI ~$92


This price gap represents the difference between a sustainable monthly SaaS expense and a luxury production cost. Choosing the $30 PixVerse Pro plan allows you to allocate the remaining $60 toward additional rendering credits or third-party editing tools.


### PixVerse character reference tool vs Runway


PixVerse includes a Character Reference (CREF) feature that allows you to lock in a subject's appearance across multiple scenes. This feature is essential for narrative continuity in your episodic content.


In contrast, Runway Gen-3 relies heavily on complex prompt engineering to maintain visual identity, which often results in character drift where a face or outfit changes slightly between clips.


Luma Dream Machine has high motion fidelity but lacks a native, one-click character-locking mechanism. This forces you to spend extra credits on iterative near-miss generations.


PixVerse’s implementation means you can produce a full storyboard with a consistent protagonist in fewer total attempts, reducing the waste of compute resources.


### Subscription flexibility and credit rollover policies


PixVerse operates on a **use it or lose it** monthly credit cycle on its standard tiers. This requires you to plan your production sprints to avoid wasting your paid capacity.


Unlike some boutique AI services that allow a percentage of credits to carry over to the following month, PixVerse resets the balance every thirty days. This means if you have a slow month, you can't stockpile resources for a busier period later.


Professional editors often use Gemini Omni Flash to automate the batch-processing of their remaining monthly credits into generic stock assets on the final day of the billing cycle. This prevents your paid value from being left on the table before the reset occurs.
